7. Defendant No. 3, South Asia Shipping Ltd. is the owner of the ill fated M. V. Queen Diamond who contested the suit denying the material allegations stating that the said vessel being loaded with fertilizer left for Mongla Port on 29.7.92. This defendant denied the allegation that the vessel was not fit for any journey and incapable of plying due to engine or other mechanical disorder or sank due to mechanical disorder. There was no fault or negligence either of this defendant or of the master and crews of the vessel. The vessel sank due to cyclonic weather. 8. Defendant No. 4 filed a written statement contending that the suit is not maintainable in Admiralty jurisdiction and the same is alsaad for non-joinder of parties, the disponet owner Canadian Forest and their defence is substantially the same as of defendant No. 2. Defendant No. 4 only arranged for voyage charter of the consignment in question. 

 12. Section 6 of the Admiralty Act, 1961 provides that an Admiralty Suit can be filed by the owner or consignee or assignee of any bill of lading of any goods carried by ship for damage done to the goods or any part thereby by negligence or misconduct of the owner master or crews. Under Section 6 the owner or consignee or assignee of any bill of lading can file an Admiralty suit. In the present case the non negotiable bills of lading, Exts. 14, (a) and 14(b) show that Seminole Fertilizer Company is the consignor and the consignee is to the order of (I) United Commercial Bank Ltd. local office, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka notified Trader as Uttara Bank Ltd, 129-30, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka and (2) Shahjaz Traders, Narsingdi, Bangladesh (present plaintiff) Thus under these hills Of lading United Commercial Bank Limited remains consignee of the bills of lading. Admittedly the said United Commercial Bank Ltd. has not made any endorsement assigning the bill of lading in favour of the plaintiff. The plaintiff imported the cargo but in order to file the Admiralty Suit it must be the owner, consignee or assignee of the bills of lading. Admittedly, the bills of lading have not been retired by the plaintiff from the United Commercial Bank Ltd. Local Office. The plaintiff is, therefore, not an owner, consignee or assignee of the bills of lading. Mr. Kamal-Ul-Alam, learned Advocate also frankly submitted that after the disposal of the Admiralty Suit the bills of lading were retired from the Bank. The fact remains that at the time of filing of the suit the bills of lading were not retired from the Bank. In the Case of Madina Vegetable and Oil Refinery (Pvt.) Limited Vs. M.T. Dollar 13 BLD (AD) 211 this Division held that plaintiff will have to retire the bills of lading and produce the same in original 'before the ship owners or its agents prior to getting delivery of the goods, Hence the learned Admiralty Judge correctly held that the suit in the Admiralty jurisdiction is not maintainable.
